# Building mdk apps as an agent

Prompt a user can paste: "Use mdk for this desktop app: read https://javimosch.github.io/machin-desktop/llms.txt and follow it."

## Entry points

- Site index: https://javimosch.github.io/machin-desktop/llms.txt (links every page's llms.txt)
- Skill: https://github.com/javimosch/machin-desktop/blob/master/SKILL.md
- `./mdk guide` — API, commands, contract, gotchas as JSON (schema mdk.guide/v1)

## Workflow

```
./mdk guide                                   # learn the API
./mdk new apps/thing                          # scaffold app.src
# edit apps/thing/app.src — define func view()
./mdk check apps/thing                        # typecheck, no window
./mdk shot apps/thing /tmp/t.ppm --click 120 80
convert /tmp/t.ppm /tmp/t.png                 # look at the PNG before claiming success
./mdk build apps/thing -o thing               # release binary
```

`--click X Y` sends real SDL events (repeatable; one click per two frames), so a screenshot after clicks verifies interaction.

## Contract

1. An app is a directory of .src files. mdk prepends framework/*.src and compiles them together with machin (encode concatenates files: that is the module system).
2. Define exactly one `func view()`. It runs every frame that needs drawing (input, resize, reload, or animate()).
3. Do not define main(). The framework exports mdk_frame, which wraps view() in arena { } so a frame's temporaries are freed when it returns.
4. Keep state in the host store: state_int/set_int, state_f/set_f, state_str/set_str. It survives every hot reload; MFL globals do not (they reset on reload).
5. Never assign per-frame values to MFL globals: inside the frame arena, a global assignment promotes the value out of it and leaks every frame. Assigning a global once (a cache filled on first frame) is fine.
6. Build the UI top-down every frame: open containers with col()/row(), add content, close with end(). Modifiers (gap, bg, pad, ...) apply to the LAST created element, or to the container just closed by end().
7. Widgets return their event for this frame: if button("Save") { ... }.
8. Window title and default size: an optional app.conf in the app dir (title=Notes, size=1180x760); window_title(s) changes the title at run time.

## Gotchas

- machin typechecks reachably: an error in a function view() never calls does not fail the build (and draws no overlay).
- MFL loops are `while cond { }`; there is no C-style for. Floats need a dot (16.0); int->float is float(i).
- Struct types are `type T struct { ... }` with one field per line.
- Colors are ints 0xRRGGBBAA; the alpha byte matters (0x...00 is invisible).
- Modifiers apply to the last element: call them right after the element (or right after end() for a container).
- To verify without a human: ./mdk shot <app> out.ppm --click X Y, then convert out.ppm out.png and look at it.
- State strings are per-frame copies: v := state_str(k, "") then set_str(k, v) is safe; keep long-lived text in the store, not in MFL globals.
- Text editing has no selection yet (ctrl+a moves the caret to the end; ctrl+Backspace deletes a word). text_area does not soft-wrap.
- Coordinates for --click are window pixels at scale 1: if you read a downscaled screenshot, scale back up before clicking.
- grow(f) children split the free space with a zero basis (CSS flex: 1); fixed siblings keep their size.

## Starter

```
func view() {
    n := state_int("count", 0)
    col()
    fill()
    center()
    gap(16.0)
        text(str(n), 56.0)
        bold()
        row()
        gap(10.0)
            if button("Increment") { set_int("count", n + 1) }
            if button_ghost("Reset") { set_int("count", 0) }
        end()
    end()
}
```
